checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection, arXiv:2607.28322v1, Sections 5.2 and C.3
checked_sources.result: Primary-source verification. The full-Gaussian point-null process is a test martingale, the exact all-start candidate-null optimization is smooth convex in Gaussian natural parameters with O(t) objective/gradient/Hessian cost, and Theorem 5.3 gives first-order high-probability delay log(A)/D_KL(Q||P) in the late-change regime. The proof uses an explicit empirical-mean/variance/predictive-score representation and compact-uniform convergence. The theorem does not itself provide an ARL-CADD expectation bound for this full-Gaussian detector.

checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, same paper, bounded-mean ARL-CADD proof in Appendix C
checked_sources.result: Primary-source contrast. The bounded-mean CADD proof controls rare bad events by combining an exponential crossing-time tail with a deterministic pathwise stopping cap. No analogous pathwise cap is supplied for the full-Gaussian detector, identifying a real uniform-integrability gap rather than a mere numerical-optimization gap.

derived_results.claim: The scalar pair-dual objective from r59 admits an O(1) exact derivative, so a safeguarded derivative-bracketing maximizer needs no numerical differentiation or Hessian.
derived_results.details: For two starts let f_i(eta)=c_i+n_i A(eta)-eta_1 S_i-eta_2 Q_i. Define Delta c=c_0-c_1, Delta n=n_0-n_1, Delta S=S_0-S_1, Delta Q=Q_0-Q_1. For lambda in [0,1], n=n_1+lambda Delta n, S=S_1+lambda Delta S, Q=Q_1+lambda Delta Q, m=S/n, v=Q/n-m^2, and h(lambda)=c_1+lambda Delta c+(n/2){1+log(2 pi v)}. Then h'(lambda)=Delta c+(Delta n/2){log(2 pi v)+m^2/v}+(Delta Q-2m Delta S)/(2v). Equivalently, by the envelope theorem h'(lambda)=f_0(eta_lambda)-f_1(eta_lambda), where eta_lambda is the Gaussian MLE for the fractionally pooled sufficient statistics. The envelope form is numerically preferable when raw sufficient statistics are large.

derived_results.claim: Concavity gives a fully certified scalar stopping rule: every sampled h(lambda) is a false-alarm-safe lower score, while tangent intersection gives a deterministic optimization-gap upper bound used only for power/computation control.
derived_results.details: h is concave because it is the infimum over eta of functions affine in lambda. If h'(0)<=0 the maximizer is 0; if h'(1)>=0 it is 1. Otherwise maintain [a,b] with d_a=h'(a)>=0>=d_b=h'(b). Concavity implies h(x)<=min{h(a)+d_a(x-a), h(b)+d_b(x-b)}. Their intersection x_U=[h(b)-h(a)+d_a a-d_b b]/(d_a-d_b) lies in [a,b], giving certified upper U=h(a)+d_a(x_U-a). Let L be the best sampled h. Then max h lies in [L,U]. Bisection on the sign of h' preserves the bracket. A coarse gap bound is U-L <= G(b-a), G=max(d_a,-d_b). False-alarm validity depends only on L, so even premature numerical stopping can only reduce power; a trustworthy U is needed only to certify the claimed approximation gap.

derived_results.claim: Only O(log log A) scalar lambda evaluations are needed per pair to preserve the source first-order detection-delay constant at threshold A, under the same compact/nondegenerate Gaussian regime.
derived_results.details: Write ell=log A. On the compact concentration event used in the source delay proof, block lengths and |h'| are O(ell). After j derivative bisections the width is 2^{-j}, hence the additive pair-score loss is O(ell 2^{-j}). Choosing j=ceil(log_2 ell)+O(1) makes this O(1)=o(ell). Replacing the exact log pair score by a lower-certified score with additive error epsilon_ell=o(ell) changes the required evidence length by only epsilon_ell/I, so the leading delay factor remains 1+o(1). With O(1) sufficient-statistic work per lambda value, a recycled K-grid implementation therefore costs O(K log t log log A) score work per monitoring time before further warm-start gains.

derived_results.claim: The two-start minimax has exact scalar strong duality under ordinary nondegeneracy; weak-dual sampled scores remain formally safe even when endpoint degeneracy prevents claiming equality.
derived_results.details: The primal inf_eta max{f_0,f_1} is the convex epigraph problem min_{eta,z} z subject to f_i(eta)<=z. Slater holds by taking any interior Gaussian natural parameter eta_2<0 and z strictly above both finite f_i values. When the pooled empirical variance is positive so the inner Gaussian fit is finite/attained, standard convex strong duality yields inf_eta max_i f_i = sup_{lambda in [0,1]} inf_eta{lambda f_0+(1-lambda)f_1}=sup h(lambda). If a tiny block has zero empirical variance, sampled feasible lambdas with positive pooled variance still provide weak-dual lower scores and therefore remain false-alarm safe; exactness should simply not be claimed for the degenerate endpoint.

derived_results.claim: The scalar pair dual extends cleanly to regular exponential families through the convex conjugate of the log-partition function.
derived_results.details: For f_i(eta)=c_i+n_i A(eta)-eta dot T_i, let n_lambda=lambda n_0+(1-lambda)n_1, T_lambda=lambda T_0+(1-lambda)T_1, c_lambda similarly. Then h(lambda)=c_lambda-n_lambda A*(T_lambda/n_lambda), whenever the pooled mean parameter is in the mean-domain interior. Bernoulli gives h=c+n H(p) with p=T/n; Poisson gives h=c+n(mu-mu log mu). Thus the same derivative bracketing and lower-certificate semantics can replace a d-dimensional candidate-null pair solve by one scalar evidence-mixing solve across a broad exponential-family class.

derived_results.claim: Fresh disjoint post-change blocks can amplify the short-block success probability, but that alone does not justify an ARL-CADD expectation claim for the full-Gaussian sparse detector.
derived_results.details: For a fixed compact neighborhood U of P, source uniform convergence implies a fresh pure-Q block of length Theta(log A) rules out all R in U with probability tending to one. Reinitializing the same predictor on disjoint post-change blocks makes these short-block events independent under iid Q, so the number of short-block retries is asymptotically geometric/tight. However detection also requires a long-context term to rule out R outside U. A rare failure of that exterior certificate can in principle contribute an unbounded amount to expectation. The source's bounded-mean CADD proof neutralizes such rare events using a deterministic pathwise stopping cap; the full-Gaussian theorem has no analogous cap. Therefore retry amplification upgrades robustness of the high-probability statement but does not by itself establish uniform integrability or CADD.

candidates_new.mechanism: For each sparse two-start Gaussian composite-null pair, maximize the exact/weak-dual scalar h(lambda) with derivative-sign bisection; threshold only the best sampled lower score and use tangent intersections solely to certify numerical suboptimality.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: O(1) work per lambda evaluation from pooled sufficient statistics; O(log log A) evaluations achieve O(1)=o(log A) additive score loss under the source compact regime, preserving the first-order D_KL delay constant. Strong duality holds under positive pooled variance; weak-dual lower scoring remains safe without it.
candidates_new.scope: New derivation/synthesis, not peer-reviewed. It applies to the two-start pathwise lower detector from r59, not to the exact all-start sum itself.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Zero/near-zero pooled variance; finite-precision overflow/cancellation; claiming an optimization-gap certificate from uncertified derivatives; assuming the high-probability delay result is already a CADD expectation result.
candidates_new.confidence: high for derivative, concavity, tangent certificate, weak-dual safety, and asymptotic evaluation count; medium-high for exact strong-dual equality at all ordinary nondegenerate endpoints

candidates_new.mechanism: Use the same scalar evidence-mixing dual and certified bracketing for Bernoulli/Poisson/other regular exponential-family pair certificates instead of solving the full natural-parameter dimension for each pair.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Formal conjugate reduction h(lambda)=c_lambda-n_lambda A*(T_lambda/n_lambda); dimension of the candidate-null inner solve disappears and only scalar lambda remains.
candidates_new.scope: Derived family-level generalization; empirical runtime/power evaluation remains open.
candidates_new.confidence: high for regular minimal exponential families with interior pooled mean parameter

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Numerical scalar optimization must converge to machine precision before thresholding can be statistically safe.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected. Every feasible sampled lambda is a weak-dual lower bound, so thresholding the best sampled h is safe immediately. Optimization accuracy affects only power/delay.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Keep lower-score safety separate from upper-gap certification.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The full-Gaussian first-order high-probability theorem already implies matching CADD after geometric block retries.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. The source theorem is high-probability only, and geometric short-block retries do not control expectation on rare failures of the long-context exterior certificate.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Need a quantitative tail/uniform-integrability argument or a valid backup detector with controlled expectation before claiming CADD.

frontier: Derive a finite-precision-safe implementation of the tangent upper certificate: stable envelope-form derivative, downward-rounded lower h values, and conservative derivative intervals. Benchmark evaluations per pair versus damped Newton on synthetic Gaussian sufficient statistics.

Seek a probabilistic replacement for the bounded-mean proof's deterministic pathwise cap: prove exponential tails for the full-Gaussian predictive-score regret plus a time-uniform exterior certificate strong enough to make the rare-event contribution to ARL-CADD uniformly integrable.

If direct CADD remains hard, construct a statistically valid backup channel whose expected delay is finite for every distinct Gaussian P,Q and show that mixing it at vanishing weight preserves the sparse full-KL first-order delay while controlling expectation tails.
Instantiate the exponential-family pair dual for Bernoulli and Poisson detectors and compare exact scalar certificates to the existing bounded-mean KL pair construction.
Resume off-policy predictable-prior/vector evidence after the Gaussian expectation-tail question is either solved or sharply bounded.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Derived an exact closed-form derivative for the Gaussian scalar pair dual.
Replaced unconstrained scalar search with a tangent-certified derivative bracket whose sampled values are safe lower evidence.
Quantified O(log log A) lambda-evaluation complexity sufficient to preserve first-order detection delay.
Closed ordinary Gaussian strong-duality regularity and generalized the pair dual to regular exponential families.
Attempted the requested CADD upgrade and isolated the remaining uniform-integrability obstruction instead of overclaiming it.

exact_next_action: Implement and numerically stress-test the certified derivative bracket on Gaussian pair sufficient statistics, including near-degenerate variances and directed-safe lower scoring; in parallel, search for a Gaussian full-detector tail argument or backup e-detector that turns the current high-probability full-KL delay into a genuine ARL-CADD bound without losing the leading D_KL constant.
